reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id, p.brand, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur > (
  SELECT AVG(p2.unit_cost_eur)
  FROM products p2
  WHERE p2.brand = p.brand
)
alternatives:
WITH brand_avg AS (
  -- one row per brand
  SELECT brand, AVG(unit_cost_eur) AS avg_cost_eur
  FROM products
  GROUP BY brand
)
SELECT p.product_id, p.brand, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
JOIN brand_avg b ON b.brand = p.brand
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur > b.avg_cost_eur

SELECT p.product_id, p.brand, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
JOIN (
  -- one row per brand
  SELECT brand, AVG(unit_cost_eur) AS avg_cost_eur
  FROM products
  GROUP BY brand
) AS b ON b.brand = p.brand
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur > b.avg_cost_eur

other_way.sql:
WITH brand_avg AS (
  -- one row per brand
  SELECT brand, AVG(unit_cost_eur) AS avg_cost_eur
  FROM products
  GROUP BY brand
)
SELECT p.product_id, p.brand, p.unit_cost_eur
FROM products p
JOIN brand_avg b ON b.brand = p.brand
WHERE p.unit_cost_eur > b.avg_cost_eur
other_way.tradeoff: A step with one average per brand, joined on the brand, makes the group plain to see but adds a GROUP BY.
